sections.h2: Which office bills a Raleigh homeowner?
sections.html:
Wake County does. Under a local agreement, its Tax Administration department sends the bills for Raleigh and the county's other towns, so a Raleigh owner receives one statement carrying county and city charges.

That department also values land, buildings and business property. Its phone line is 919-856-5400 and its email is taxhelp@wake.gov. The county tax bill pages also say Wake has 16 cities and towns, and a municipal rate is folded into each bill. Questions about how Raleigh set its own rate go to the city, not the county.

sections.h2: What rates apply to a Raleigh property tax bill?
sections.html:
Wake County's rate page prints a county rate of .5371 and a Raleigh rate of .3720, for a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Wake's 2026 bill page says county commissioners voted on June 1 to adopt a fiscal year 2027 budget that raises the county rate to 53.71 cents.

The county's own worked example for a house inside Raleigh and outside any fire or special district adds a $20 waste reduction fee. Your bill may add more, depending on where the parcel sits:

  • Residential waste reduction fee, charged per living unit, so a duplex has two.
  • Fire district tax, where the property lies in one.
  • Special district tax, usually a downtown area designated by legislation.
  • Municipal fees such as stormwater or solid waste.
  • A vehicle fee for motor vehicles inside a municipality.

To see the exact charges for your address, use the county's online bill search or call the tax office.

sections.h2: When are Raleigh property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in July. Each one covers the fiscal year that starts July 1 and ends the next June 30. Payment at face amount is allowed from September 1 through January 5, as G.S. 105-360.

After that, interest runs. Wake's real estate page prints 2 percent for January and an added 0.75 percent per month after that. The county says it takes partial payments in any amount, with no prior approval, as long as the balance is paid in full by January 5. Short-term payment plans are possible, and the county advises calling early because it cannot help once a bill is overdue. Past-due taxes can be collected from paychecks, bank accounts or rent under state law.

sections.h2: Who gets billed when a Raleigh home changes hands mid-year?
sections.html:
The county explains it by sale date. If you sold between January and June and keep no interest in the property, the July bill should go to the new owner, who is responsible for paying it.

If the sale falls after the July bill and before the January delinquency date, the county mails a statement for the unpaid tax to the new owner, and the seller may disregard the original notice. A tax lien attaches to Wake real estate on January 1 and stays until all the tax is paid. Owners who paid through a mortgage escrow account the year before do not receive a July bill, so look up the account online. Ask the closing attorney how the year's bill will be split and settled, and ask Wake County Tax Administration for the balance.

sections.h2: Can Raleigh owners get a tax break?
sections.html:
Wake County names three state programs: senior and disabled, tax deferment, and disabled veteran. The county's tax relief pages explain who qualifies, and its 2026 bill page says the June 1 state deadline has passed but late applications can be accepted for good cause through December 31, 2026. Not knowing the program existed is typically not good cause.

The underlying laws are the senior and disabled statute and the veteran statute. Wake County Tax Administration can say whether a window is open.

sections.h2: How can you pay a Wake County tax bill in Raleigh?
sections.html:
Online, by several routes. The county's 2026 bill page lists ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Visa, Mastercard, American Express and Discover cards. Bills can be looked up online without waiting for the mail.

Owners who pay through mortgage escrow are not mailed a bill and are encouraged to look online or call 919-856-5400. After each partial payment, Tax Administration sends a statement showing what remains.

sections.h2: When does Wake County revalue Raleigh property?
sections.html:
Wake's latest countywide revaluation carries a January 1, 2024 effective date, and the next one is dated January 1, 2027. In March 2025 the Wake County Board of Commissioners voted to phase in a two-year cycle, so the first revaluation on that cycle is effective January 1, 2029.

The county says it divides about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods by market, economic and geographic conditions. Appraisers price land and buildings from sales data, review the results in the field and the office, and compile them into a Schedule of Values that commissioners must approve. The state minimum is one revaluation every eight years, and the county says shorter gaps keep value increases from arriving as one large jump.

sections.h2: Which values and rates sit behind the bill due September 1, 2026?
sections.html:
The county explains that bills due September 1, 2026, and delinquent after January 5, 2027, rest on assessed values as of January 1, 2024, and the rates approved in June 2026. Bills due September 1, 2027 use values as of January 1, 2027 and the rates set in June 2027.

  • A bill is assessed value times a rate stated per $100 of value.
  • Revaluation changes values only. Elected county and town officials set the rate.
  • State law has local governments publish a revenue-neutral rate for comparison, though they need not adopt it.
  • The county's online real estate search shows your current value and the data behind it.

sections.h2: What if my Wake County value or property record looks wrong?
sections.html:
The county plans to mail 2027 value notices in the week of January 19, 2027, when commissioners receive the results. Every owner may appeal to the county's board of equalization and review, and instructions plus a portal link are due out in January 2027.

If the record itself is wrong, for example the wrong square footage or a removed outbuilding, file the county's online request form with your address or account number and any documents. An appraiser may need to visit, and you would be contacted. Tax Administration also plans a comparable sales tool in January, useful as evidence. After the local board, the state Property Tax Commission is the next level, per G.S. 105-290.

sections.h2: How should a Raleigh seller deal with unpaid property tax?
sections.html:
Get the balance in writing from Wake County Tax Administration and hand it to your closing attorney. An unpaid bill follows the house, so it has to be settled for the title to be clean.

If you are behind, the sale can clear it from your proceeds. Another option is a payment plan before the January deadline. A direct cash purchase of a Raleigh house as-is can move quickly while interest runs. Whoever buys, have the payoff quote cover the day you close.

faqs.q: Will Raleigh mail me a separate city tax bill?
faqs.a: No. A local agreement has Wake County collect the city's share together with its own, so the single bill comes from Wake County Tax Administration.

faqs.q: When does a late Raleigh bill begin to accrue interest?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6 if the bill is not paid in full by January 5. The county prints 2 percent for January and 0.75 percent per month after that.
Yes. Any partial amount is welcome with no prior approval, so long as the full balance is in by January 5. Payment plans are possible if you call early.

faqs.q: What rates are printed for Raleigh on the Wake County page?
faqs.a: The county rate page prints .5371 for Wake County and .3720 for Raleigh, a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Fees and district taxes may add to your bill, so check your own account.

faqs.q: Who owes the July bill if I sold my Raleigh house in the spring?
faqs.a: If you sold between January and June and keep no interest, the county says the new owner should receive the July bill and is responsible for paying it. Confirm at closing.
